extraction.name: C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models
extraction.description: C-EVAL is a comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It comprises 13,948 multiple-choice questions across 52 diverse disciplines at four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional. It also includes C-EVAL HARD, a subset of challenging subjects requiring advanced reasoning.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He
extraction.publisher: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.citeAs: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, et al. C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. arXiv:2305.08322v3, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from mock exams freely available on the internet, past exam questions from top universities in China publicly shared by students, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website (with authorization).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The primary source is mock exams freely available on the internet. Additionally, college-level questions come from past exam questions from top universities in China, and a minor fraction from the Weipu website.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were parsed from PDF or Word documents into structured format. For subjects with complex mathematical notations, manual conversion to LaTeX was performed. Questions with fewer than four options were eliminated; for questions with more than four options, incorrect choices were randomly dropped. Deduplication and cleaning were applied. All questions underwent several rounds of human validation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For the development split, explanations were generated by prompting GPT-4 to produce step-by-step explanations, which were then manually revised by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Labels of the test split are kept private to ensure fair use. Users submit model predictions to https://cevalbenchmark.com to obtain test accuracy, where a public leaderboard is maintained.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: C-EVAL, along with all English-language benchmarks, is far from perfect for LLM evaluation. There are many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, as well as aspects beyond accuracy including safety, bias, and robustness.
